title: TypeScript Classes & Access Control: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision notes on TypeScript class member visibility, readonly, parameter properties, abstract classes, implements, static members and structural typing of classes.

chapters.title: Class Members and Visibility Mental Model
points: TS class members default to public; modifiers public, private, protected are compile-time checks only and are erased in emitted JS
public: accessible anywhere (inside class, subclasses, outside instances)
private: accessible only inside the declaring class; subclasses and outside code get a compile error
protected: accessible in the declaring class and subclasses, but not via an instance from outside
Example: class A { private x = 1; protected y = 2; z = 3 } then new A().x and new A().y error, new A().z works

chapters.title: #private, readonly and Parameter Properties
points: #name is a JS runtime-private field (ES2022): inaccessible outside the class even in plain JS, unlike TS private which is erased
private vs #private: private can be bypassed with obj['x'] or a cast; #x cannot, and also cannot be accessed with brackets
readonly: property can be assigned only in its declaration or in the constructor; later assignment is an error, and it is shallow (readonly arr: string[] still allows arr.push)
Parameter property: constructor(private readonly id: string, public name = 'x') {} declares and assigns the field in one line, no body needed
Gotcha: a modifier on a constructor parameter (public/private/protected/readonly) is what makes it a property; a plain parameter stays a local variable

chapters.title: Abstract Classes and implements
points: abstract class cannot be instantiated with new; it can hold concrete members plus abstract members (no body) that subclasses must implement
Concrete subclass must implement all abstract members or it must be declared abstract too; example: abstract area(): number;
implements checks a class against an interface or type shape at compile time only; it inherits nothing and emits no JS
extends inherits implementation (single base class only); implements can list many: class C extends Base implements A, B {}
Gotcha: implements does not infer parameter types from the interface, so method params in the class need explicit annotations; abstract classes exist at runtime (instanceof works), interfaces do not

chapters.title: Static Members and Structural Typing of Classes
points: static members belong to the class constructor, not instances: Counter.count, accessed via the class name and not this-instance
Static members can be public/private/protected/readonly and are inherited by subclasses; static blocks static { ... } run once at class load
Classes are typed structurally: any object with the same shape is assignable, so const p: Point = { x: 1, y: 2 } works when Point is a class
Exception: a class with a private or protected member becomes nominal-like; only that class or its subclasses are assignable, even if the shape matches
Instance type vs constructor type: Point is the instance type, typeof Point is the constructor type with its static side

chapters.title: Common Mistakes with Classes
points: Believing private gives runtime security: it is erased, so use #private for real privacy
Forgetting readonly is shallow: it does not freeze nested objects or array contents
Calling new on an abstract class, or leaving an abstract member unimplemented in a concrete subclass
Using a method as a callback loses this (onClick={obj.method}); fix with an arrow-function property or .bind
Assuming two classes with the same public shape are distinct types: structural typing makes them interchangeable unless a private member exists

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Class Modifiers
points: Visibility: public (anywhere) | protected (class + subclasses) | private (class only) | #x (class only, runtime enforced)
readonly: set in declaration or constructor only, shallow
Parameter property: constructor(private readonly x: T) {} declares and assigns the field
abstract class: no new, abstract members need no body, subclasses must implement them
implements I, J: shape check only, multiple allowed; extends B: inheritance, one only
static: lives on the class, use ClassName.member, inherited by subclasses
Structural typing: same shape means assignable; a private or protected member makes the type nominal-like
